items.question: What must happen before an old region can safely regain authority after failover?

section_new.excerpt: ## Write authority and the recovery contradiction A secondary region can serve read-only degraded traffic before it can safely become a writer. Promoting writers requires a policy for **in-flight acknowledgments**, replica lag, ordering, globally unique identifiers, replay idempotency and a recovery model when the former primary returns. An active-active system further requires conflict rules that match domain semantics; last-write-wins may be unacceptable for some mutable state. A fictitious acceptance exercise should stage two adversarial states: a write acknowledged in A but not visible in B when the failover begins, and a stale client still sending mutations to A after B has been promote
